title: Roman Councils deny absolute god-cult of images, yet require relative cult of Christ, Mary, and saints
source_text: I. Ex iis quae Thesibus praecedentibus allata sunt, liquido patet, Concilia Ecclesiae Romanae, non docere quidem ullas imagines habendas esse pro diis, aut aliquam virtutem iis esse tribuendam, ob quam coli debeant cultu summo atque absoluto: eadem tamen concilia constanter statuere imagines, non solum Christi, sed etiam Deiparae Virginis, & reliquorum Sanctorum aliquo cultu dignas esse, non propter se, sed propter exemplar quod repraesentant.
pass_a_gloss: From the things that were brought forward in the preceding Theses, it is clear that the Councils of the Roman Church do not indeed teach that any images are to be held for gods, or that any virtue is to be attributed to them on account of which they ought to be cultivated with the highest and absolute cult: yet the same Councils constantly establish that images, not only of Christ, but also of the God-bearing Virgin, and of the remaining Saints, are worthy of some cult, not on account of themselves, but on account of the exemplar which they represent.
pass_b_english: Roman Councils refuse to call images gods or to vest them with absolute, highest cult.
Yet they steadily require some cult of Christ’s, Mary’s, and the saints’ images—for the prototype, not for the image as such.

lemmas.gloss: with the highest and absolute cult
